\section{Hypercontractivity --- Randomization --- Projection Bounds}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Randomization.ProjectionBounds
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Randomization --- Projection Bounds: Introduction}
Walsh coefficients of randomization identify product components with sign-cube Fourier coefficients. Spectral identities and self-adjoint norm duality support the product low degree projection bounds.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Randomization --- Projection Bounds: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of randomization]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_fourier_coefficient}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, DecisionTree.fourierCoeff_sum_chiS}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space, fix an outcome $x$, and let
$S\subseteq[n]$. The Walsh--Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the function $r\mapsto
R_rf(x)$ is the $S$-component of $f$ evaluated at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a low degree Fourier projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_has_degree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the Boolean
cube. Every nonzero Fourier–Walsh coefficient of the Fourier truncation of $f$ to sets
of size at most $k$ is indexed by a set of size at most $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Norm contraction of a low degree projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_l2_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the Boolean
cube with the uniform probability measure. The $L^2$ norm of the Fourier truncation of
$f$ to sets of size at most $k$ is at most the $L^2$ norm of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Higher moment bound for a low degree projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_projection_noise_ge_two}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_has_degree, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_l2_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_two, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.l2Norm_noiseOp_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_norm_ge_two, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lp_norm_mono, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $q,\rho\in\mathbb R$
satisfy $q\ge2$ and $0<\rho\le1$. On the Boolean cube with uniform measure, the
$q$-moment norm of the Fourier truncation of $g$ to sets of size at most $k$ is at most
$(\sqrt{q-1}/\rho)^k$ times the $q$-moment norm of the noise operator with parameter
$\rho$ applied to $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of the product moment norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.product_norm_const_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega_i$ be its outcome space. For every
$q>0$, every $a\ge0$, and every function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, the product moment norm
satisfies $\|af\|_{q,P}=a\|f\|_{q,P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrated randomization norm bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.randomizationNorm_le_of_pointwise_cube_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_rpow, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomizationNorm, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly
positive atom masses, and let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on its outcome space. If
$q>0$, $A\ge0$, and for every outcome $x$ the uniform-cube power mean of $r\mapsto
R_rf(x)$ is at most $A$ times that of $r\mapsto R_rg(x)$, then the joint power mean over
product outcomes and uniform cube points satisfies $\|Rf\|_q\le A\|Rg\|_q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Components of a low degree projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.component_lowDegree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.lowDegree, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_component}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega_i$ be its outcome space. For every
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, every $k\in\mathbb N$, every function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb
R$, and every $x\in\Omega$, the $S$-component of the low degree projection of $f$ at $x$
equals the $S$-component of $f$ at $x$ when $|S|\le k$, and equals zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomization commutes with noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.randomization_cube_noise}

product noise transform of $f$ at $x$ equals applying the Boolean-cube noise operator
with parameter $\rho$ to the function $r\mapsto R_rf(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomization and low-degree projection]

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjointness of the low degree projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.product_lowDegree_selfAdjoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.lowDegree}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega_i$ be its outcome space. For every
$k\in\mathbb N$ and functions $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $\mathbb E_P[(f^{\le
k})g]=\mathbb E_P[f(g^{\le k})]$, where $f^{\le k}$ and $g^{\le k}$ denote the low
degree projections and $\mathbb E_P$ is expectation under the product mass.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjoint norm bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.product_selfAdjoint_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteNorms.selfAdjoint_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.product_norm_const_mul}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly
positive atom masses, and let $T$ be an operator on real-valued functions on its outcome
space. Suppose $T$ is self-adjoint with respect to product expectation, meaning $\mathbb
E_P[(Tf)g]=\mathbb E_P[f(Tg)]$ for all functions $f,g$. If $q>1$, $A>0$, and
$\|Tg\|_{q/(q-1),P}\le A\|g\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ for every $g$, then $\|Tf\|_{q,P}\le
A\|f\|_{q,P}$ for every $f$.
\end{theorem}
